title: Convert a short controlled forward entry into horizontal takeoff.
brief: The two-step bilateral approach jump is the priority. A one-leg long-jump plant, a walking box entry, height-oriented alternating bounds and a reverse-lunge drive each constrain how the legs organize an incoming body; an overhead forward throw couples a step to a longer arm lever.

explosive.name: Two-step Approach Broad Jump
explosive.job: Redirect a small amount of forward entry momentum through a two-foot takeoff.
explosive.cue: Take exactly two controlled forward steps into a two-foot plant, swing the arms and jump forward; hold the bilateral finish 2 s.
explosive.regress: Slow/shorten the entry; stop if braking or an extra shuffle replaces the plant.
explosive.note: 12 entry steps total; each entry at most 2 m.

explosive.name: One-step Long Jump to Two-foot Landing
explosive.job: Use a single-foot plant after entry while gathering into a bilateral finish.
explosive.cue: Take one controlled step onto the takeoff leg, drive the free knee/arms forward and jump from that foot; land on two feet and hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Slow the step and shorten travel; stop for a buckling plant or a feet-first reach.
explosive.note: Four ordinary entry steps total, each at most 1 m.

explosive.name: Walk-in Two-foot Box Jump
explosive.job: Organize a moving two-foot plant into an elevated full-foot receiving position.
explosive.cue: Walk two short steps into a two-foot gather, then jump forward/up onto a low box and hold 2 s; step down to reset.
explosive.regress: Lower the box and slow entry; stop for a rushed plant, clipping or partial-foot landing.
explosive.note: Four ordinary walking entry steps total; each two-step entry at most 2 m.

explosive.name: Alternating Bounds for Height
explosive.job: Preserve a useful upward component while carrying forward momentum from one leg to the next.
explosive.cue: Use four controlled alternating bounds with a tall trunk, upward free-knee drive and short forward travel; hold the final contact.
explosive.regress: Reduce height/step length; stop for reaching the foot or losing the tall hip position.
explosive.intent: Controlled upward projection with modest forward travel
explosive.note: Four landings, two each leg; at most 4 m. This is not a distance-bound score.

explosive.name: Step-in Forward Overhead Medicine Ball Throw
explosive.job: Time a forward step with a long-lever two-arm release.
explosive.cue: Start with a light ball above the forehead, take one short forward step and extend the arms to release ahead while ribs remain controlled; keep a stable finish.
explosive.regress: Use lighter load and a shorter arm excursion; stop for lumbar arching or throwing outside verified containment.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support
explosive.note: Four ordinary step-ins total; no athlete jump.

explosive.name: Reverse-Lunge Drive Jump to Two-foot Landing
explosive.job: Convert a rear-step loading action into a lead-leg drive and balanced finish.
explosive.cue: Step back into a shallow reverse lunge, drive through the front foot as the rear knee comes forward and make a modest forward/up jump; land on two feet and hold.
explosive.regress: Shorten the lunge and flight; stop for rear-foot slipping, a twisting push or uncontrolled landing.
explosive.note: Four ordinary rear entry steps total; no running approach.

control.name: Wall Drive Iso Hold
control.job: Lightly maintain trunk/shin alignment in a forward-driving plant position.
control.cue: Use a verified fixed wall or immovable high support, lean as a straight body line and hold one knee raised while the stance heel stays comfortably lifted.
control.regress: Use a more upright angle and less pressure; stop for lumbar sag or calf strain.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

control.name: Lateral Step-Down
control.job: Control frontal-plane pelvis/knee position while a single leg receives the approaching body.
control.cue: Stand on a low stable step, lower the free heel toward the floor beside the step for 3 s and rise in 1 s without pushing from that heel.
control.regress: Lower step height/load; stop for pelvic drop or loss of the whole stance foot.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

strength.name: Hip Thrust — pelvic dumbbell, upper back on bench
Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs

decision: Forward-entry tasks replace stationary drills rather than increasing their prescribed run-up distances and calling that novelty. Bilateral versus single-foot plant and floor versus box receiving geometry are explicit differences; height-oriented bounds use a different impulse direction and are not compared with distance bounds. Step-up becomes the lead strength task for controlled forward weight transfer; the bilateral squat is omitted from the six selected lifts to avoid unnecessary knee-extension volume. New step-up loads start from demonstrated handling and reserve, not from previous squat weights.
next_job: Class 10 will address receiving a small imposed drop and projecting forward; it requires separate demonstrated rebound competence and recovery.
